analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is a harness-specific lifetime bug: fuzzer_request_shutdown() manually releases EG(exception) via zend_object_release() before normal php_request_shutdown(). That early release can destroy a live Generator object referenced from symbol table/other shutdown roots. Later, shutdown_destructors() walks EG(symbol_table) and zval_call_destructor() reads refcount from the same zval/object, causing heap-use-after-free in zend_gc_refcount(). So the vulnerability is not in zend_gc_refcount() itself, but in premature exception object destruction in the fuzzer shutdown path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires script execution that leaves EG(exception) set to an exception object graph that (directly/indirectly) references a Generator involved in cyclic/self-referential structures (as in PoC: generator send/self-reference plus thrown/caught invalid class). During fuzzer_request_shutdown(), EG(exception) is released first, freeing that object graph; then php_request_shutdown() runs normal destructor/symbol-table cleanup and touches stale zvals, yielding UAF.
